title: fix(runtime, service-automation): a job's connector pull reads its mapping from the package that declares the job (ADR-0150 D3)
body:
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB15UT19uwZoigv8upT552L7)_ Fixes #32071 Clause-②: no (narrowing) Narrowing: first-party count 0 for each (no example app or first-party package declares a job `pull`). (1) D3 (c): a job in one package body pulling a mapping only another body of the same artifact declares, with no dependency between them, goes from pulled through that mapping to refused `outside-closure` (409 naming the holder); fix: declare the dependency, or keep job and mapping in one package. (2) A job in a package body pulling a mapping filed under the artifact's top level (no body declares it; the top-level id is no package) goes from pulled to refused `outside-closure` naming the top-level id; fix: move the mapping into the job's body, or the job to the top level (no dependency can reach a top-level id). (3) A job name two or more package bodies declare, met by name (a JSON-loaded artifact's top-level copies): its pull read with no package; each run is now refused before any call or write, 409 naming every declaring body, never attributed to the first body; fix: rename the job in all but one package. D3 (a) cannot be reached through the binder: it schedules a pull only when the artifact itself declares the mapping; a direct `pullConnectorSource` call naming a package can reach it (pinned). Why `no`: the one widening answer (409 → the job's own mapping) only undoes Part A's 409, which is unreleased and superseded in this same release (Part A's changeset is still pending), and the two optional members on exported types (`ConnectorPullOptions.callerPackageId`, `ConnectorPullDeps.mappingByPackage`) are additive. Metadata-protocol: none Skills-docs: updated here — `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx` says which mapping a job's pull reads; `skills/**` has no job-pull or `callerPackageId` text (`git grep -i callerPackageId -- skills/` is empty) Part B of #32071 under epic #31527 (ADR-0150), after PR #32117 (Part A) and PR #32114 (#32078, `ConnectorSourcePullRequest.callerPackageId`). Claim amendment with the step-0 rulings: Q1 the per-job declaring body, Q2 an injected registry resolver. ## 维护者速读 - 改了什么：job 绑定器在每次 pull 时把声明该 job 的包作为 `callerPackageId` 传给 automation 服务（多包工件里是 job 所在的包体；没有包体声明的顶层 job 不属于任何包，不传包，照旧走无包读）；connector pull 按 ADR-0150 D3 从这个包读 mapping：自己的，否则依赖闭包里唯一的持有者，否则 409 拒绝。停用包的 mapping 在这条路径上照旧答 404。 - 为什么改：Part A 之后，两个包同名 mapping 时 pull 一律 409；现在 job 能读到自己包的那一个。闭包外的 mapping 不再被静默借用。 - 风险与回滚：第一方受影响 0 处（没有示例声明 job pull）。不带包的 pull 行为不变。两处收窄（闭包外的包体 mapping、顶层残余 mapping）都有可执行的修法。回滚即 revert。 - 先看：`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts` 的 `jobDeclaringPackages`，再看 `packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts` 第 1 步。 - 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation exec vitest run src/connector-pull.test.ts`，预期 46 条全过。 - 需要你做的：无，席位落地。 ## What changes - **`packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts`**: new `jobDeclaringPackages(bundle, appId)`. The binder's jobs are the artifact's resolved `jobs`, flattened across `packages[]` with no package on them, and the job service keys all of them under the top-level `appId`. The declaring body is found by walking `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`, as `AppPlugin` finds a datasource's owner: a body's job object answers that body (by identity, else a top-level copy of it by name in body order); a top-level job no body declares is the residual, whose owner id is no package (`recordResidualOwner`), so it names no package unless a body carries that id; an artifact without `packages[]` declares every job from `appId`. Each pull run now calls `pullConnectorSource({ mapping, context, callerPackageId })`, leaving `callerPackageId` out for a residual job. - **`packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts`**: `ConnectorPullOptions` gains `callerPackageId`, and `ConnectorPullDeps` gains an optional `mappingByPackage`. A caller of a package reads the mapping from it: its own mapping, else the one holder in its declared closure plus `sys`. A refusal (two holders in reach, only a holder outside the closure, or only the environment) fails the pull with the refusal's own code, status and sentence, reason `mapping_name_refused`, before any call or write. A pull naming no package (absent, `null`, `''`), or a composition with no registry to ask, keeps Part A's protocol read. - **`packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-package-scope.ts`**: `mappingNameResolver(ctx)`, the `connectorNameResolver` precedent for `mapping`: `resolvePackageScopedName(objectql.registry, { type: 'mapping', name, callerPackageId })`, read at question time. Not `getMetaItem({ packageId })`: that is the D5 exact qualifier and would refuse a closure holder. The answer is then given as the served face gives it on `main` (#24210, applied after resolution): a resolution reaching a disabled package's item (the caller's own, or the one closure holder), or an `outside-closure` refusal naming exactly one holder that is disabled, answers not-found, so the pull answers `404 MAPPING_NOT_FOUND` as the no-package read does. `packageScopedHoldersOf` is untouched (#32183 changes it), so a disabled holder beside an enabled one in the closure still counts and is refused, as today. **`plugin.ts`** injects it into the pull's deps. - **`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`** (carrier item 3, TSDoc only): the absent `callerPackageId` no longer reads "exactly as today"; it says the no-package read is D3's (the environment's own mapping, else the one package holder; two holders refused), that a top-level job no body declares sends no package, and that a disabled package's mapping is not found. The doc pin in `automation-service.test.ts` moves with it and refuses the old phrase. - **`content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`**: which mapping a job's pull reads (a residual top-level job reads with no package; the reach is the transitive dependency closure), the remedy for a refused one where it applies, and that a disabled package's mapping is answered missing. - **`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts`** (module doc only, carry from the review): only a pull that names no package reads through the protocol with no package. ### What moves (first-party count 0 for each) 1. A mapping name two packages hold, the job's package one of them: FROM `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming both (Part A) TO the job's own package's mapping. A widening. 2. **BREAKING**, D3 (c): a job in body A pulling a mapping only body B declares, A not depending on B: FROM pulled through B's mapping TO refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` (`outside-closure`) naming B, and the run fails. The fix: declare the dependency in A's manifest, or keep the job and the mapping in one package. 3. **BREAKING**, the mirror of the residual case: a job in a package body pulling a mapping filed under the artifact's top level (a mapping no body declares, filed under the top-level id, which has no package row): FROM pulled TO refused `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` (`outside-closure`) naming the top-level id. Measured over a real registry. No dependency can name a top-level id, so the fix is to move the mapping into the job's package body, or move the job to the top level, where it reads with no package and is pulled (pinned). 4. **BREAKING** (epic red-line R1): a job name two or more package bodies of one artifact declare (`composeStacks` concatenates `jobs`), met by name, as every JSON-loaded artifact's flattened top-level copies are: FROM a pull with no package TO each run refused before any call or write, `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming every declaring body. `jobDeclaringPackages` answers a refusal for it, never the first body in package order. Fix: rename the job in all but one package. 5. D3 (a): a package caller whose name only the environment holds is refused naming the environment. Not reachable through the binder (above). A direct in-process `pullConnectorSource` call naming a package reaches it; no first-party caller does. One refusal becomes a miss, nothing pulled either way: a job whose own package is disabled, with a second, enabled holder of the same name, goes FROM `409 mapping_name_refused` (Part A's unreleased answer) TO `404 mapping_not_found` (its own item is step 1, then withheld as disabled). Pinned, and in the changeset. Unmoved, and pinned: a residual top-level job names no package, so it pulls a body's mapping or a top-level mapping as on `main`; a disabled package's mapping (the caller's own, the one closure holder, or the one holder outside the closure) answers `404 mapping_not_found` on both paths. Step 0 listed "own item over a same-named environment item" as a further move; the seat withdrew it. Measured, it does not move: a runtime row stored under a package mapping's name is that mapping's overlay (ADR-0005; the registry says so at registration), so the package caller's own item IS the row, as the no-package read's is. Pinned as a CONTROL. The changeset carries the same list, `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and a "Supersedes, in the same release" line for Part A's entry, which said the pull did not yet read `callerPackageId`. ## Why Part A made a two-holder mapping name a refusal at every reader that names no package. The pull named none, because the job's package did not reach it: #32078 added the request key, and this PR has the binder send it and the pull read by it. Each job now reads the mapping its own package means, and no longer reaches across an artifact into a body it does not depend on. ## Tests - **`connector-pull.test.ts`**, new describe over a real `SchemaRegistry` and `mappingNameResolver` (each holder's mapping pulls its own path, so the path the action got says which mapping was read): - two holders, the caller one of them: each caller pulls its own (no package: 409); - D3 (c): the only holder outside the caller's closure is refused naming it, no call, no write (no package: that holder is pulled); - D3 (a): an environment-only name is refused for a package caller (no package: the environment's own); - the one holder in the declared closure is pulled; - a disabled own mapping beside an enabled holder: its caller gets `404` (no package: `409`); - a disabled package's mapping answers `404 mapping_not_found` for its own caller, for a caller whose one closure holder it is (and is pulled again once re-enabled), and as the one holder outside the closure; the no-package answer beside each is the same; - CONTROL (#32183's class): a disabled holder beside an enabled one in the closure still counts, refused naming both, as the no-package read is; - residual owner: a no-package pull (a residual job's) pulls a body's mapping and a top-level mapping; MIRROR: a body's caller pulling a top-level mapping is refused naming the top-level id; - CONTROL: a runtime row over a package's mapping is served to both callers alike; `callerPackageId` absent, `null` or `''` reads by no package; no registry to ask reads by no package. - **`app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts`**: a single-package job names the app; on a multi-package artifact a body's job names its body, a top-level copy of it too, and a residual top-level job no package (unless a body carries the top-level id); a residual job's run sends no `callerPackageId`; two bodies each declaring job `sync`, loaded as JSON top-level copies: every run is refused 409 naming both bodies and no pull is asked for; the existing sibling-body test now asserts the run names `com.example.jobs`. - **Forced test change**: eight existing assertions of the pull request shape in the same file gain `callerPackageId: APP_ID`. - **`automation-service.test.ts`**: the doc pin reads the new absent-value sentence and refuses "exactly as today"; it also reads that a residual top-level job sends no package and that a disabled package's mapping is not found. ## Verification **Head 1d77d18f on main 326453eb** (merged in as a merge commit, no rebase). Two merges since 1e4267bd. 32dd04f7 merged main b2c0202f cleanly. 8482fb3b merged main e883c71f; it conflicted in the `plugin.ts` import block against #32257, and both sides were kept. 1d77d18f merges main 326453eb with two hand edits: - the PR's multi-line `@objectstack/core` import already carries `artifactPackageId` and `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`, so main's (#32333) single-line import of the same names is dropped in `app-artifact-handlers.ts` (it was a TS2300 in the merge queue); - #32339's new job-pull test now expects `callerPackageId: APP_ID` in the pull request, the same forced shape as this PR's earlier assertion edits. #32339 wires the windowed datasource reader behind `pullOnce` step 1 (`if (isPlainObject(artifact.datasourceSource)) return pullDatasourceSource(…)`). A `datasourceSource` pull therefore reads its mapping by the declaring package exactly as a connector pull does: the same refusal and the same disabled-holder withholding. Contract delta record 6782556520 judged this. On 1d77d18f, under `os-verify-lock`: - `turbo build --force` of service-automation, runtime and their dependencies exits 0, including the runtime DTS build; `check-dts-emitted` passes. - Typecheck: runtime and service-automation exit 0. - Runtime `app-artifact-handlers*`: 94 passed. - Service-automation full suite: 275 files, 3713 passed. - Cloud-connection `marketplace-install-local-jobs`: 17 passed. Cli `package-install-local-jobs-pull.integration`: 8 passed. - Eslint on `app-artifact-handlers.ts` exits 0. Earlier heads: Head 1e4267bd on main 7575116c (merged in, no rebase, no conflict). The head before it, 924c58ca, merged main 842086478; that merge conflicted in `connector-pull.ts` because #32275 moved `ConnectorPullError` and its reason union into `pull-refusal.ts`. The resolution takes main's structure, carries the `mapping_name_refused` TSDoc fix into `pull-refusal.ts`, and keeps `pullOnce` step 1 as this PR wrote it. At that head #32275's windowed datasource reader had no caller (#32339 has since wired it; see above). On this head (every heavy run under `os-verify-lock`, after a full `turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs`): - `@objectstack/runtime` full suite: 579 files, 9677 passed (19 skipped). Targeted: runtime `app-artifact-handlers.job-pull` + `.jobs`, service-automation `connector-pull.test.ts`, cloud-connection `marketplace-install-local-jobs.test.ts`, cli `package-install-local-jobs-pull.integration.test.ts`: each exit 0. - Typecheck of runtime and service-automation: exit 0. `pnpm lint`: exit 0. - Gates: `dispatch-gates --commands` derived 117 families; all 117 exit 0; `--ran` 117 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED. On 924c58ca: service-automation full suite 272 files / 3657 passed, spec typecheck and the spec doc pin green, gates 117/117, CI green on every non-skipped run. On dfc7a7de: full dogfood battery exit 0 (448 / 3 files, 3739 / 42 tests), objectql and dogfood typecheck exit 0.
Ablations (each via scripts/ablation-replace.mjs, restored; git diff --exit-code HEAD exit 0 after each batch) 1. The binder passes `appId` instead of the declaring body: runtime 2 red (the sibling-body run names `com.example.jobs`; a residual job's run names no package). 2. The pull ignores `callerPackageId` (no package read): service-automation 5 red (two holders → own, D3 (c), D3 (a), the closure holder, the residual mirror). 3. The pull drops the package read's refusal: service-automation 4 red (D3 (c), D3 (a), the #32183-class CONTROL, the residual mirror). 4. The spec TSDoc says "exactly as today" again: spec 1 red (the doc pin). 5. The resolver stops withholding a disabled holder: service-automation 4 red on 924c58ca (own disabled, own disabled beside an enabled holder, closure holder disabled, sole outside holder disabled). 6. A residual job names `appId` again: runtime 2 red (the `jobDeclaringPackages` unit pin and the residual run). 7. The spec TSDoc says a residual job sends its top-level id: spec 1 red (the doc pin). 8. A job name two bodies declare answers the first body again: runtime 1 red (the two-bodies `sync` pin). Ablations 2 to 4 ran on dfc7a7de, 5 and 7 on 924c58ca, and 1, 6 and 8 on this head (1 is now 3 red: sibling body, the two-bodies `sync` pin, the residual run; 6 is 2 red).
## Acceptance notes - `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx` is a docs edit outside the first ruled file surface, made because the paragraph Part A wrote ("a pull cannot yet read its own package's mapping") turned false with this change. - Nits 7 and 8 of the contract review stay as they are, by the seat's ruling: a `callerPackageId` of `sys_metadata` or `__runtime__` takes the registry path (the resolver reads it as no package; no binder sends either), and a deterministic D3 refusal still fails the run and is retried by `retryPolicy`, as in Part A. ## Human Minimum - [x] 1.
